root_cause: The feature-detection-based dispatch logic for selecting the RISC-V vector ChaCha20 implementation checked only CPU capability flags (RISCV_HAS_ZBB, riscv_vlen, RISCV_HAS_ZVKB) and input length, but never validated pointer alignment of the `out`/`inp` buffers before invoking vector load/store based assembly routines that require (or strongly prefer) aligned accesses on real hardware.
findings: ChaCha20_ctr32() on riscv64 selects the vector/Zbb (and optionally Zvkb) assembly implementations of ChaCha20 purely based on length and CPU feature flags (RISCV_HAS_ZBB(), riscv_vlen() >= 128, RISCV_HAS_ZVKB()). It never checks whether the `out` and `inp` buffer pointers are aligned to the machine word size. The RISC-V vector assembly routines (ChaCha20_ctr32_v_zbb / ChaCha20_ctr32_v_zbb_zvkb) us
